# Install snippets

The four ways to put the widget on a page, exactly as the developer docs show them. The script tag suits any site; the npm packages suit bundlers; the React wrapper adds a provider and a button component.

## Script tag

One tag before `</body>`, with the project's publishable key. The widget loads its settings from Opem and shows the Help button.

```html file=script-tag.html
<script
  src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js"
  data-project="pk_live_…"
  defer
></script>
```

## ESM with a bundler

`@opem/browser` exports the same `Opem` object as the script tag. Call `init` once on the client.

```ts file=esm.ts
import { Opem } from "@opem/browser";

Opem.init({ projectKey: "pk_live_…" });
```

## React provider

`@opem/react` wraps `init` in a provider; children can use `useOpem()`.

```tsx file=react/app.tsx
import { OpemButton, OpemProvider } from "@opem/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <OpemProvider projectKey="pk_live_…">
      <OpemButton>Help</OpemButton>
    </OpemProvider>
  );
}
```

## A React button that opens a request

`OpemButton` opens the panel; `useOpem()` gives the API for your own components.

```tsx file=react/report-button.tsx
import { useOpem } from "@opem/react";

export function ReportButton({ report }: { report: string }) {
  const opem = useOpem();
  return (
    <button
      onClick={() =>
        opem.open("request", {
          kind: "problem",
          title: `${report} did not export`,
        })
      }
    >
      Report a problem
    </button>
  );
}
```
